source: Original 84 operational-risk case IDs are preserved as GT-prefixed IDs. 63 regressions add confirmed pricing, explicit synthetic policies and tutor self-service controls.

priority_policy.P0: Blocks release of the affected feature and every full-product release until implemented and passed with evidence.
priority_policy.P1: Required for the promised in-scope workflow. Blocks its milestone completion when failing or unexecuted.
priority_policy.P2: Lower-urgency behavior. Keep its feature disabled or explicitly defer it if implementation and verification are incomplete.

cases.title: Guardian claims an unlinked student

given: GuardianB has no active relationship with LearnerA.
when: Require the student’s verified consent before linking the guardian to bookings, documents or receipts.

assertions: An unlinked guardian receives no student data through either search or a direct link.

cases.title: Guardian consent expires or is revoked

given: GuardianA has an active link to LearnerA and queued deliveries before revocation.
when: Recheck authorization at each request and cancel active sharing links and queued guardian deliveries.

assertions: After revocation, the guardian cannot open the next export or upload another receipt.

cases.title: Guardian books for two siblings

given: GuardianA has separately approved relationships with LearnerA and LearnerB and a distinct enrollment for each.
when: Bind the payer, attending student and selected seat separately before taking payment or accepting uploads.

assertions: A file for the first sibling never appears on the second sibling’s seat.

cases.title: Guardian forwards a student invitation

given: A single-use invitation is bound to GuardianA and has an explicit expiry.
when: Bind a single-use invitation to the intended account and reject expired, reused or forwarded invitations.

assertions: A second account cannot activate the same invitation or acquire guardian privileges.

cases.title: Student opens another member’s link

given: LearnerA and LearnerB belong to the same group with separately owned receipts and private feedback.
when: Check membership and document scope on every request, including direct links to group seat records.

assertions: Another member’s receipt, private attachment and attendance note each return access denied.

cases.title: Staff access changes mid-session

given: AgentA has a signed-in session and permission that AdminA subsequently revokes.
when: Apply current roles immediately, including to already signed-in staff and outstanding export requests.

assertions: A demoted agent cannot approve a refund using an existing browser session.

cases.title: Returning customer changes contact details

given: LearnerA has a stable customer UUID, historical bookings and a newly verified synthetic contact.
when: Verify the new contact and match a stable account identifier before updating the existing customer.

assertions: An approved phone change preserves prior bookings without creating or merging another account.

cases.title: Two students request one private slot

given: Two learners target the same available TutorA private interval and both meet the fixture confirmation policy.
when: Reserve the instructor and time in one operation and offer alternatives to the unsuccessful student.

assertions: Concurrent requests create exactly one confirmed private booking and one occupied instructor slot.

cases.title: Two students claim the last seat

given: A forming group has one remaining seat after counting all unexpired holds.
when: Check capacity and reserve the seat in one operation, including active holds in the count.

assertions: One seat remains available to only one requester and confirmed seats never exceed capacity.

cases.title: Same student retries a group booking

given: LearnerA submits the same enrollment command repeatedly with one Idempotency-Key.
when: Reuse the original request and enforce one active enrollment per student in each group meeting.

assertions: Repeated clicks return the original seat, with one invoice and one payment request.

cases.title: Private and group teaching times overlap

given: TutorA has a confirmed group interval that overlaps a requested private interval by ten minutes.
when: Check the instructor’s complete schedule, including overlapping durations, before confirming either format.

assertions: A private session overlapping the last ten minutes of a group is rejected.

cases.title: Seat hold expires during checkout

given: A seat hold expires and another eligible learner claims the capacity before a late transfer settles.
when: Release expired holds and recheck capacity before allocating any late matched payment to a seat.

assertions: Late money remains recorded even if the freed seat has already been sold.

cases.title: One group member cancels their seat

given: A confirmed group has independently paid enrollments and the draft cancellation policy is explicitly selected.
when: Cancel that enrollment and apply its refund terms while preserving the instructor’s meeting and other seats.

assertions: Only one seat reopens and all remaining students retain their meeting access.

cases.title: Admin reduces capacity below confirmed seats

given: A group has capacity four and three confirmed enrollments.
when: Block the reduction until staff explicitly resolve the affected enrollments and notify those students.

assertions: Reducing capacity four with three confirmed seats to two returns HTTP 409 and preserves every enrollment.

cases.source_adaptation: The legacy capacity example is resized to the confirmed two-to-four-person pricing tiers while retaining its invariant and ID.

cases.title: A waitlisted seat becomes available

given: A configured waitlist has two eligible synthetic learners in a deterministic order.
when: Notify the next eligible student and start a time-limited offer under the configured queue policy.

assertions: An expired offer passes to exactly one next student without increasing capacity.

cases.title: Local time skips or repeats

given: The timezone adapter supplies a skipped local time and a repeated local time from its pinned timezone database.
when: Store the Cairo time zone and resolved instant. Ask staff to resolve ambiguous or nonexistent times.

assertions: A daylight-saving test either rejects the time or records the explicitly chosen occurrence.

cases.title: Student reschedules near a cutoff

given: A fixture policy sets a server-side rescheduling cutoff and the clock is controllable.
when: Evaluate the configured cutoff on the server and record the policy version and decision time.

assertions: Requests a minute either side of the example cutoff follow the configured outcomes.

cases.title: Two staff reschedule one meeting

assertions: One update wins and the other sees the saved time before retrying.

cases.title: One student requests another group time

given: LearnerA has a paid group seat and an eligible seat exists in another occurrence.
when: Offer a transfer to an available seat and keep the original group meeting intact.

assertions: Only the requesting student changes groups, with the agreed fee difference recorded.

cases.title: Instructor is suddenly unavailable

given: TutorA becomes unavailable with future assignments and a separately completed occurrence.
when: Suspend new bookings, identify affected meetings and ask staff to arrange cover or new times.

assertions: All affected meetings have an owner and previously completed sessions stay unchanged.

cases.title: Series changes after some meetings finish

given: A series contains a completed occurrence and future occurrences.
when: Apply edits to the selected occurrence or future occurrences and preserve historical attendance and charges.

assertions: A future-series time change leaves the completed occurrence and its statement unchanged.

cases.title: Reminder is queued before rescheduling

given: An old reminder is durable in the outbox when the occurrence schedule version changes.
when: Replace scheduled reminders and check the current meeting time and status immediately before delivery.

assertions: The old reminder is suppressed and each participant receives one current reminder.

cases.title: Meet creation times out after success

given: The fake calendar provider creates the event and then times out before returning its successful response.
when: Retry with the same request identifier and reconcile the calendar event before creating another.

assertions: After a simulated timeout, both portals display the same single event and Meet link.

cases.title: Calendar authorization expires before class

given: Calendar credentials expire for an upcoming confirmed occurrence.
when: Alert operations, reconnect the authorized account and allow staff to publish a verified replacement link.

assertions: Both portals show the approved replacement and one change notice reaches each participant.

cases.title: A group member leaves the roster

given: LearnerD is removed from a group and retains a previously received invitation.
when: Remove portal access, update attendees and use host admission controls or a fresh restricted link.

assertions: The removed member cannot retrieve the link or enter using the old invitation.
The configured real provider admission and invitation behavior passes an explicit provider contract test before production enablement.

cases.title: Upload contains unsafe or oversized content

cases.title: Network drops during preparation upload

cases.title: Student uploads a private group question

assertions: Simultaneous CS confirmations produce one balance change, one audit entry and one receipt of confirmation.

cases.title: Customer sends several partial payments

given: A customer charge is 50000 minor units and independently settled transfers are 30000 and 20000.
when: Apply each verified installment to its seat and enforce the configured threshold for confirming attendance.

assertions: Payments of 300 and 200 settle a 500 seat exactly once.

cases.title: Transfer exceeds the seat fee

given: A customer charge is 50000 minor units and an independently settled transfer is 55000.

assertions: A 550 transfer settles a 500 fee and leaves 50 identifiable as customer credit.

cases.title: Customer replaces an unreadable receipt

given: Receipt version one is unreadable and LearnerA uploads a new version.
when: Version the attachment, preserve uploader and submission times, and restart review against the latest version.

assertions: The new reviewer sees version two and both attachments remain in the audit history.

cases.title: Proof appears plausible but details conflict

given: The receipt is present but the receiving account, amount or settled-transfer evidence conflicts.
when: CS flags inconsistencies for review and contacts the authorized payer without changing the confirmed balance.

No customer allocation or booking confirmation is posted when a required reconciliation prerequisite is missing.

cases.title: Payment credited to the wrong seat

when: Admin reverses the misallocation with a reason and reapplies the same transfer to the correct seat.

cases.title: A group seat needs a refund

given: One group enrollment has settled payments and multiple concurrent refund requests could exceed them.
when: Admin authorizes the amount against that seat and its settled payments, then Finance records disbursement.

assertions: Refunding one group member leaves other balances intact and total refunds within the paid amount.

cases.title: Bank reverses a settled transfer

given: The provider reverses a transfer that already funded an enrollment.
when: Record the reversal against the original payment, reopen the debt and flag any related refund.

assertions: The reversed amount leaves net collections once and a second reimbursement is blocked.

cases.title: Group attendance posts more than once

given: One three-person group occurrence is completed and its completion event is delivered twice.
when: Create one payable per completed group meeting under its saved fee rule, independent of attendance retries.

assertions: Three attendees and two completion messages create exactly one occurrence-level payable of 62500 minor units.

cases.title: Instructor rate changes after booking

given: An occurrence has a saved fee agreement before the tutor default is updated.

assertions: Updating the instructor’s default rate leaves the agreed fee on existing sessions unchanged.

cases.title: Instructor receives a partial payout

given: TutorA has 25000 earned and 15000 settled payout minor units.
when: Allocate each confirmed payout to earned fees and carry the unpaid amount into the instructor’s statement.

assertions: On 250 earned and 150 paid, the statement shows 100 still owed.

cases.title: Payout destination or method changes

given: TutorA proposes a new synthetic payout destination with an unverified ownership state.
when: Verify the payee and approved bank account, InstaPay address or wallet before releasing the payout.

assertions: A newly supplied wallet stays blocked until an authorized reviewer verifies its ownership.

cases.title: Payout transfer times out mid-send

given: A payout send times out and the provider outcome is initially unknown.
when: Hold the payout pending, check the provider reference and retry only after confirming a failed transfer.

assertions: The unknown payout blocks another send. A provider-confirmed settlement posts once with no additional wage expense.

cases.title: Booking and CRM updates arrive together

given: Verified customer fields exist before concurrent and out-of-order booking and register events arrive.
when: Update the same customer by stable identifier and preserve earlier values when incoming fields are blank.

assertions: Repeated or out-of-order events produce one customer and retain the verified contact details.

cases.title: Two customers share a phone

given: LearnerA and LearnerB have separate identities and share one synthetic family contact.
when: Flag possible duplicates for staff review. Keep separate student identities and require evidence before merging records.

assertions: A shared family number alone never merges siblings, their attendance or their payments.

cases.title: Support archives an inactive customer

given: An inactive customer has linked bookings and immutable financial records.
when: Hide the record from ordinary search, preserve authorized financial history and log any reactivation.

assertions: Archived customers disappear from outreach lists and their linked ledger entries remain traceable.

cases.title: Staff exports beyond their permission

given: GuardianA requests an export including LearnerA and an unrelated customer.
when: Apply the user’s role and current record scope to each export. Exclude unrelated students and receipts.

assertions: An export requested by a guardian contains only the linked student’s authorized information.

cases.title: Customer field starts with a formula

given: Synthetic text fields begin with equals, plus, minus or at-sign spreadsheet formula prefixes.
when: Escape spreadsheet formula prefixes in exported text fields while preserving the original stored value.

assertions: An exported name beginning with an equals sign opens as text in a spreadsheet.

cases.title: Records change during paginated export

given: A large export starts at a fixed snapshot and new records are committed between pages.
when: Export from a fixed snapshot and use stable ordering and cursors to process each page.

assertions: Adding a booking mid-export causes no duplicates or omissions against the starting snapshot.

cases.title: An export link is forwarded

given: GuardianA forwards an export URL to GuardianB after the export is created.
when: Require current authorization, expire download links, and log requester, scope, row count and download time.

assertions: An unauthorized recipient cannot download the file and the denied attempt is recorded.

cases.title: A meeting is marked complete

given: A group occurrence is ready for completion but one enrolled learner has unmarked attendance.
when: Require session ID, instructor, actual times, topic, roster and individual attendance before creating an immutable completion record.

assertions: Completing a group without attendance for one enrolled student returns a validation error.

cases.title: Attendance is disputed after completion

given: A signed-off occurrence exists before an authorized attendance correction is requested.
when: Append an authorized correction with old and new values, evidence, author and reason. Preserve the signed-off record.

assertions: The original roster remains readable and the corrected report points to the amendment.

cases.title: A session summary reaches the wrong audience

given: A group summary and LearnerA-specific feedback share an occurrence but have different audiences.
when: Store public teaching notes separately from individual feedback and authorize delivery against the intended audience.

assertions: One group summary reaches its roster while personal feedback reaches only its intended student.

cases.title: Provider outage delays payment verification

given: Receipts and transfer notifications arrive while independent verification is unavailable.
when: Queue receipts and incoming records durably, show pending status and resume matching after the service recovers.

assertions: A provider outage creates no confirmations and recovery processes each queued item once.

cases.title: Notification delivery repeatedly fails

given: A required reminder repeatedly fails and its delivery worker later restarts.
when: Retry on a bounded schedule, then alert the assigned owner with the latest delivery status.

assertions: A failed reminder becomes an actionable item and restarting delivery sends it once.

cases.title: Restore follows a database outage

given: A verified checkpoint and subsequent committed events exist before a simulated database outage.
when: Restore a tested backup, replay later committed changes and reconcile bookings, seat counts and ledger balances.

assertions: Restored totals match the verified checkpoint plus replayed events, with no duplicate payouts.

cases.title: Daily close exposes an unexplained variance

given: A synthetic statement variance remains unexplained at daily close.
when: Reconcile channel statements, collections, refunds and payouts. Assign unresolved differences to Finance and retain supporting records.

assertions: A seeded variance remains open with an owner until an evidenced adjustment resolves it.

cases.title: An operation changes session or payment status

given: A payment confirmation and a tutor-assignment event use different configured recipient rules.
when: Select recipients from the configured event matrix and resolve the acting student, guardian, instructor and staff roles.

assertions: A payment confirmation reaches the payer while instructor assignment reaches only the assigned instructor.

cases.title: Guardian access changes after email queuing

given: GuardianA has an authorized queued message when the relationship is revoked.
when: Recheck consent and the current verified address immediately before sending any student-specific email.

assertions: Revoking consent after queuing results in zero deliveries to the former guardian.

cases.title: A group change emails the roster

given: A group change targets multiple learners with distinct emails and private seat data.
when: Send notices individually and include only the recipient’s own seat information and authorized session details.

assertions: Inspect two messages. Neither contains another member’s address, payment, attendance or personal feedback.

cases.title: An operation emits duplicate email events

given: One notification event is replayed five times across worker restarts.
when: Record one delivery per event, recipient and channel, and reuse it after worker restarts.

assertions: Replaying the same confirmation five times generates one message per intended recipient.

cases.title: Customer changes their email mid-booking

given: LearnerA verifies a replacement email after a transactional notification is queued.
when: Verify the new address before activation and recheck the active address for queued transactional mail.

assertions: A queued receipt notice reaches only the newly verified address after the change.

cases.title: A required notice hard bounces

given: A required notice hard bounces before an authorized contact correction and resend.
when: Flag the delivery for its owner. Permit authorized staff to resend after correcting the verified address.

assertions: The failure stays visible until resolved and one authorized resend is logged.

cases.title: Provider delivery callbacks arrive out of order

given: Authentic provider delivery events arrive duplicated and out of order.
when: Verify callback authenticity, deduplicate provider event identifiers and avoid reverting a confirmed delivery to an earlier state.

assertions: Repeated delivery and earlier queued callbacks leave a single delivery marked delivered.

cases.title: Customer opts out of marketing

given: LearnerA opts out of promotional mail while remaining eligible for operational notices.
when: Honor optional communication settings separately from approved operational notices and trigger only the applicable email type.

assertions: An opted-out student receives their rescheduling notice and receives zero promotional messages.

cases.title: One lead sends several inquiries

given: One verified lead has three separate inquiry events.
when: Keep all interactions in the lead history and count each eligible lead ID once per cohort.

assertions: Three messages from one verified lead yield one lead and three interactions.

cases.title: Lead inquiry crosses a reporting cutoff

given: The first eligible inquiry belongs to January in Cairo and the eventual booking belongs to February.
when: Use the first eligible inquiry timestamp in Cairo and apply the same observation window to each cohort.

assertions: A late booking stays with its original lead cohort and retains its own booking date.

cases.title: One guardian enquires for two siblings

given: GuardianA enquires for two separately linked learners who later have individually recorded attendance.
when: Verify the guardian relationship, link each attendee separately and leave ambiguous student matches pending review.

assertions: One guardian lead can produce two distinct learners only after both attend.

cases.title: Attendance or payment events replay

given: Checkout and completed-present attendance events are replayed for one stable student identity.
when: Deduplicate incoming event IDs and enforce one first attendance per student across all sources and formats.

assertions: Replaying checkout and attendance events leaves the qualified student count unchanged.

cases.title: Returning student attends a new campaign session

given: One student has prior lifetime attendance and a different newcomer is absent.
when: Check lifetime attendance across private and group sessions. Qualify only a student’s first completed, attended session.

assertions: A returning attendee and an absent newcomer add zero to newly taught students.

cases.title: The lead lacks tracked campaign identifiers

given: One lead self-reports a social source without a tracked paid touch and a second has verified organic provenance.
when: Keep self-reported sources separately. Assign verified organic traffic to organic and leave untraceable traffic unassigned.

assertions: A self-reported Instagram lead without a tracked ad stays outside verified paid conversions.

cases.title: Overlapping campaigns receive late engagement events

given: Two campaigns have overlapping eligible touch windows and a delayed event has an earlier event time.
when: Apply the documented attribution window and tie rule using event times. Record any change to previously reported credit.

assertions: A delayed touch may reassign one conversion but never credits both campaigns.

cases.title: A cohort has no new students

given: Three cohorts have zero students, confirmed zero spend or missing spend respectively.
when: Calculate acquisition cost from matched cohort spend and newly taught students. Preserve missing or zero spend distinctly.

assertions: Zero students yields no CAC. Confirmed zero spend with one qualifying student yields zero.

cases.title: The bot cannot resolve an inquiry

given: A synthetic inquiry remains unresolved after the configured FAQ attempts.
when: Offer human support, create one queue item and attach the relevant conversation and attempted answers.

assertions: An unresolved request creates one open handoff and adds one to the backlog.

cases.title: A human takes over the conversation

given: An automated reply is queued while AgentA claims the conversation for human support.
when: Pause automated replies, cancel pending bot sends and resume only after staff explicitly ends the handoff.

assertions: A follow-up during handoff reaches the assigned agent and generates no bot reply.

cases.title: An outbound reply misses the service window

given: A free-form reply is attempted 25 hours after the last inbound message under a fixture 24-hour service window.
when: Outside 24 hours from the last user message, require an approved template and valid opt-in before sending.

assertions: A free-form reply at hour 25 is blocked even when an agent retries.

cases.title: Recipient withdraws consent ahead of dispatch

assertions: An approved promotional template queued before opt-out produces no outbound message afterwards.
The production adapter verifies the configured provider policy and callback contract independently of the local fake-provider fixture.

cases.title: Shared number requests a student’s private details

given: A shared family contact requests private details without a verified learner relationship.
when: Verify the recipient’s identity and authority, then direct them to a protected record for sensitive information.

assertions: A sibling using the same number receives neither the student’s receipt nor attendance details.

cases.title: Two agents claim the same handoff

given: Two agents concurrently claim one unassigned handoff.
when: Assign the conversation in one operation and update queue totals only when the assignment succeeds.

assertions: Simultaneous claims result in one owner, one active case and one workload increment.

cases.title: Handoff arrives when agents are offline

given: A handoff arrives outside configured staffed hours.
when: Keep the handoff queued, show staffed hours and preserve its waiting time until an agent accepts.

assertions: An overnight request remains open at shift start with its original arrival time.

cases.title: WhatsApp webhooks repeat or arrive late

given: Authentic WhatsApp callbacks repeat and arrive in a different order.
when: Verify event authenticity, deduplicate message and status identifiers, and apply delivery updates in order without reopening work.

assertions: Replaying a delayed notification creates neither a second reply nor another queue item.
The production adapter verifies the configured provider policy and callback contract independently of the local fake-provider fixture.

cases.title: Two-person tier uses exact seat and occurrence amounts

given: The approved two-person tier is selected.
when: Calculate the customer quote and the privileged contribution independently.

assertions: Each seat is 57500 minor units. The occurrence has one tutor fee.

cases.title: Three-person tier preserves fee endpoints and exact approved fee

given: The three-person tier allows an internal fee from 60000 through 65000.
when: Quote all seats and compute the contribution for each exact approved fee.

assertions: The fee range remains internal. Every calculation uses integer minor units.

cases.title: Four-person tier preserves fee endpoints and exact approved fee

given: The four-person tier allows an internal fee from 70000 through 75000.
when: Quote four seats and compute the contribution for each exact approved fee.

cases.title: Unsupported group tier fails without a fallback price

given: Only the approved two, three and four-person group tiers are configured.
when: Request a group quote for zero, one or five participants and an unsupported currency.

assertions: Each unsupported request returns a validation error. No tier is guessed and no charge is created.

cases.title: Range alone cannot approve the occurrence tutor fee

given: An occurrence has a configured compensation range but requires a specific agreement.
when: Approve fee agreements with a missing fee, a fractional minor unit, out-of-range fees and valid boundary fees.

assertions: Missing, noninteger and out-of-range fees fail atomically. Approved agreements store one exact integer fee and policy version.

cases.title: Forming group changes from two to three under a versioned proposal

given: Two learners hold quote version one under the draft formation policy.
when: Add the third learner and issue quote version two.

assertions: The new seat price is 55000. Old acceptances remain historical. Every affected authorized booker and the assigned tutor must accept the current version and AdminA must approve before atomic confirmation. Quote changes create no money event.

cases.title: Forming group changes from three to four under a versioned proposal

given: Three learners hold quote version two under the draft formation policy.
when: Add the fourth learner and issue quote version three.

assertions: All affected authorized bookers and the assigned tutor must accept the current version. AdminA commits confirmation atomically against its approved fee and price snapshot. Historical quotes and money allocations remain intact.

assertions: Exactly one command commits. The other receives a conflict and no balance becomes negative.

cases.title: Reservation retry reuses the original entitlement movement

given: A reservation command has a stable idempotency key and enrollment ID.
when: Replay the command and submit an equivalent duplicate enrollment request.

assertions: One active reservation holds 1000 quanta. Replays return its ID and leave the balance unchanged.

cases.title: Expired hold releases reserved credit once

given: A 1000-quanta reservation belongs to an expired enrollment hold.
when: Run the expiry worker twice and replay its event after restart.

assertions: Append one release movement. All 3000 quanta become available and no credit is consumed or cash created.

cases.title: Completed attendance consumes the reserved credit exactly once

given: A valid controlled completion references one active 1000-quanta reservation.
when: Deliver the completion event twice through separate database connections.

assertions: One consume movement replaces the reservation. Recognize 50000 from package liability without an additional customer receipt.

cases.title: Cancellation before delivery releases credit under the selected policy

given: The enrollment holds 1000 quanta and has no consumption entry.
when: Cancel under the explicitly selected draft restoration policy and retry.

assertions: Release the held quantity once. Keep the original reservation and cancellation history. No earned tuition or cash refund is invented.

cases.title: Post-consumption correction preserves the original credit event

given: An authorized correction determines that the consumed service was not delivered.
when: Apply the credit-restoration branch with a reason and stable remedy ID.

assertions: Append one restore entry and one recognition reversal. Preserve the original consumption event. Replays have no extra effect.

cases.title: Approved half delivery uses exact credit and fee quantities

given: The draft policy and authorized completion explicitly select 500 consumed quanta, 500 released quanta and an exact approved tutor earning.
when: Complete the 30-minute delivered occurrence against its 60-minute base duration.

assertions: Consume 500 quanta, release 500 reserved quanta, recognize 25000 customer tuition and accrue the explicitly approved 36250 tutor earning. Retain the 72500 original fee agreement and its -36250 approved adjustment.

cases.title: Partial delivery without an approved remedy remains pending

given: Actual duration differs from the base duration and no applicable approved partial-delivery decision exists.
when: Attempt financial finalization using elapsed time alone.

assertions: Keep the occurrence in completion_pending. Create no automatic fractional credit consumption, earning or refund until the required decision is recorded.

cases.title: Renewal transfer moves quantity and value atomically once

given: The source and target packages belong to LearnerA and the source has sufficient available credit.
when: Execute and replay the same 1500-quanta transfer, including a crash between the two proposed writes.

assertions: Either both transfer entries commit or neither does. Replays leave one transfer pair. Combined credit and unearned value remain conserved.

cases.title: Transfer cannot exceed available unreserved credit

given: A source has 3000 remaining quanta with 2000 already reserved.
when: Attempt to transfer 1500 quanta while another request changes a reservation.

assertions: Transfers use available unreserved credit inside the transaction. An over-limit request returns a conflict with no partial transfer.

cases.title: Package lineage rejects cycles and unauthorized owner changes

given: A transfer lineage already runs from package_source to package_target.
when: Attempt the reverse cycle, a self-transfer and a transfer to another learner without an explicitly supported authorization.

assertions: Each invalid lineage command is rejected before posting credit or value entries.

cases.title: Renewed label cannot discard remaining delivery obligations

given: A package has unused credit and is linked to a successor.
when: Change its workflow label to renewed without recording a transfer or consumption.

assertions: Remaining credit and unearned value stay visible in the obligation report. The label alone posts no entitlement or money movement.

cases.title: Cash refund and restored credit share one remedy value cap

given: One affected consumed credit has a 50000-minor-unit remedy value.
when: Race the full cash-refund and full credit-restoration branches using the same remedy scope.

assertions: At most one full-value branch commits. The sum of cash and restored credit value cannot exceed 50000. Replays preserve the first authorized result.

cases.title: Non-divisible package value reconciles at final consumption

given: The selected synthetic package policy allocates sequential consumption from remaining lot value and remaining credit quanta, with a final residual.
when: Consume the equal and uneven portions and separately allocate the stable-ordered batch using exact integer rational arithmetic.

assertions: Sequential equal portions recognize 33333, 33334 and 33334 from 100001. Sequential uneven portions of a 100000 package recognize 33333, 16666 and 50001. Batch largest remainder allocates 33334, 33334 and 33333 from 100001. Each mode conserves the package value exactly.

cases.title: Expired package follows the stored eligibility policy

given: The test package has an explicit expiry and the clock is after it.
when: Request a new reservation and separately inspect pre-expiry confirmed reservations.

assertions: The new ineligible reservation fails. Existing reservations follow the stored approved policy rather than an implicit blanket deletion. Credit expiry creates auditable movements only for eligible unreserved quantities.

cases.title: Cancellation and completion serialize on the same package reservation

given: Cancellation and completion both read the same enrollment and reservation version.
when: Race cancellation release against completion consumption.

assertions: One versioned transition wins. The loser sees a conflict and must reload. The reservation is consumed or released once, with credit and recognition matching the winning state.

cases.title: Concurrent review claims produce one case owner

given: The review case is unassigned at version one.
when: AgentA and AgentB claim it simultaneously.

assertions: One current claim commits, one conflict is returned and only the winning agent receives an active workload assignment.

cases.title: Expired or stale review claims cannot resolve the case

given: A claim lease expires or another authorized action advances the case version.
when: Resolve using the expired claim or old expected_version.

assertions: Return HTTP 409 and preserve the current owner, evidence version, allocation and balance.

cases.title: Receipt replacement invalidates an in-flight old-version approval

given: AgentA reviewed receipt version one before LearnerA uploads version two.
when: Race replacement against a resolution referencing version one.

assertions: The transaction checks the current eligible evidence version. A stale approval cannot allocate against superseded evidence and must reload the case.

cases.title: Quarantined or unscanned evidence cannot authorize payment

given: The independent transfer is settled but the receipt is quarantined or its scan is incomplete.
when: Try to resolve as AgentA and AdminA and to download the unsafe file.

assertions: Both approval paths fail the same prerequisite. No customer credit or confirmation is posted and unsafe content is unavailable.

cases.title: Role revocation is checked inside payment resolution

given: AgentA claimed the case while authorized and keeps a valid authentication token.
when: Revoke the staff membership before the resolving transaction authorizes its command.

assertions: Current database membership denies the command. Token age or an earlier claim cannot preserve approval power.

cases.title: Ambiguous reconciliation remains owned and unresolved

given: Evidence could match multiple incoming transfers or its receiving-account details conflict.
when: Record needs_information or escalate with an owner and reason.

assertions: Preserve all evidence and candidate matches. The queue state is actionable and customer paid balance stays unchanged.

cases.title: External transfer identity includes channel and receiving account

given: Two valid transfers share an external reference string across different receiving accounts.
when: Ingest both and replay each within its original composite identity.

assertions: Store two distinct transfers and deduplicate only exact channel, receiving-account and external-ID repeats.

cases.title: Concurrent allocations cannot exceed the settled transfer remainder

given: One settled transfer has 50000 unallocated minor units and two eligible claims each request 50000.
when: Allocate both claims concurrently.

assertions: Total active allocations remain 50000 or less. One full claim succeeds and the other becomes a conflict or exception.

cases.title: Authorized split payment preserves separate learner balances

given: GuardianA has active relationships to both learners and a verified 100000 transfer explicitly covering two 50000 charges.
when: Approve the explicit allocation plan for both charges.

assertions: Allocate 50000 to each learner with separate allocation IDs. Retain one bank transfer and do not duplicate cash.

cases.title: Unmatched settled cash remains separate from booking approval

given: The bank evidence establishes a settled 50000 transfer while customer proof is missing.
when: Ingest settlement, attempt approval and replay ingestion.

assertions: Record cash and an unmatched obligation once. Booking allocation remains zero until eligible proof and authorization exist.

cases.title: Review resolution and its outbox commit together

given: A valid resolution will post allocations, audit history and a confirmation notification.
when: Inject a failure before commit and then retry after worker restart.

assertions: The failed transaction leaves no partial balance, resolved flag or outbox entry. The successful retry commits one complete outcome and one confirmation event.

cases.title: Reversal and allocation races conserve net funds

given: A 50000 settled transfer is eligible for allocation when the provider reports its reversal.
when: Run allocation and reversal in both controlled transaction orders.

assertions: The final net collection is zero. The charge remains owed 50000. A committed allocation has a linked reversal and an allocation attempted after reversal is rejected.

cases.title: Cancelled occurrence with money already paid creates a resolution obligation

given: A cancelled occurrence has a 45000 settled tutor advance and no approved cancellation fee.
when: Rebuild earnings, payables and the exception queue.

assertions: Keep cash outflow and the unresolved advance visible. Cancellation alone creates no earned fee and no additional payout.

cases.title: Future booking cannot establish attendance or acquisition

given: The clock precedes the occurrence start and the student has no earlier attendance.
when: Attempt completion, present attendance finalization and acquisition-event publication.

assertions: Reject future completion and retain unmarked attendance until the permitted workflow. No new-student qualification or earning is produced.

cases.title: Unknown payout is reconciled before any additional send

given: A provider timeout leaves the durable payout attempt unknown.
when: Retry user actions and workers, then deliver a settled provider result twice.

assertions: No new payout request is sent while the outcome is unknown. The settled result creates one cash posting and settles the original payable once.

cases.title: Finance report reconciles to the primary ledger

given: All synthetic receipts, deliveries, liabilities and disbursements are posted.
when: Build cash, receivable, package, tutor and earned-result reports from primary entries.

assertions: Cash reconciles to receipts less disbursements. Outstanding obligations and earned result reconcile to 130000 without using an action label as an accounting source.

cases.title: Refunding overpayment reduces cash and credit without changing tuition

given: The 50000 charge is settled and the remaining 5000 belongs to the customer.
when: Approve and settle a 5000 surplus refund, then replay the provider result.

assertions: Reduce customer credit and cash once. Keep the original charge and tuition recognition unchanged.

cases.title: Tutor advances do not hide another tutor payable

given: TutorA has 62500 earned and 72500 paid while TutorB has 45000 earned and zero paid.
when: Build per-tutor statements and the overall obligation report.

assertions: Show TutorA advance 10000 and TutorB payable 45000 separately. A net 35000 display cannot replace the gross payable and advance amounts.

cases.title: Later inquiries preserve the original cohort and lifetime student status

given: A stable learner has an earlier eligible inquiry and prior lifetime completed-present attendance.
when: Receive a new inquiry, contact update and later campaign booking.

assertions: Preserve the original first eligible inquiry and its January cohort. The later inquiry adds an interaction and creates no newly taught student.

cases.title: Unknown provenance and verified organic remain different buckets

given: One inquiry has only a self-reported source and another has verified organic provenance.
when: Classify attribution and compute verified paid conversions.

assertions: Unknown provenance stays unassigned, verified organic stays organic and neither becomes a paid conversion. Missing source evidence is retained explicitly.

cases.title: Exports preserve non-additive occurrence fees and conversion ratios

given: A joined report has two participant rows for one occurrence and two cohort ratio rows.
when: Export detail and build totals at their declared grains.

assertions: Count the occurrence tutor fee once in authorized internal reports. Recompute conversion from summed valid numerator and denominator. Customer exports exclude fee and margin columns entirely.

cases.title: Package cash remains unearned until the approved delivery event

given: A funded package exists before any controlled completion.
when: Compare reports immediately after purchase, after reservation and after one approved consumption.

assertions: Purchase and reservation retain 150000 contract liability with zero earned tuition. One consumption recognizes 50000 and leaves 100000 liability. Cash is unchanged by reservation and consumption.

cases.title: Public website remains responsive and bilingual-ready

given: The public pages use approved brand assets and locale-aware layout components.
when: Exercise primary navigation and actions at 320,768 and 1440 widths with LTR and pseudo-RTL fixtures.

assertions: Approved content remains legible, primary actions are keyboard reachable and pages have no horizontal overflow. Localized strings and direction changes do not alter authorization or monetary values.

cases.title: Anonymous catalog reads expose only approved complete offers

given: Approved, draft and incomplete-policy offers coexist.
when: Request catalog records anonymously through the public read interface and attempt direct table access.

assertions: Only the approved complete offer is returned through an explicit allowlist. Draft or incomplete offers and privileged financial fields remain inaccessible.

cases.title: Fixture and acceptance manifests remain synthetic and traceable

given: The implementation loads the two versioned JSON manifests from this pack.
when: Validate IDs, requirements, priorities, layer enums, task IDs, fixture references and synthetic identity domains.

assertions: Every original 84 case ID occurs once. All 18 requirements have coverage. Identities use example.test and every monetary oracle uses integer minor units or an explicitly invalid input variant. Unsupported evidence cannot mark a test passed.

cases.title: Synthetic seeding is repeatable and idempotent

given: An isolated development database, schema or transaction uses deterministic UUID mappings and synthetic identities.
when: Apply the same seed twice and compare IDs, journal counts, balances and relationship scopes.

assertions: The second seed creates no duplicate identities, credits, receipts, obligations or outbox messages. A clean reseed produces the same canonical snapshot.

cases.title: Clean migrations enforce the private database boundary

given: An empty ephemeral PostgreSQL database is available with anonymous and authenticated test roles.
when: Apply all migrations from scratch and inspect effective schema, table, sequence and function privileges.

assertions: Private finance and secret tables have no browser grants. Only intended sanitized reads and authenticated command interfaces are exposed. Reset and reapply reproduce the same security boundary.

cases.title: Production rejects synthetic fixtures and unverified provider readiness

given: The local fixture envelope is marked synthetic and fake providers are configured.
when: Attempt production publication, outbound dispatch and release readiness approval with the fixture envelope or missing required provider evidence.

assertions: The production boundary rejects synthetic publication and fake outbound delivery configuration. Required provider capabilities and completed release evidence must be present before the real feature is enabled. Local simulated publication remains usable for end-to-end tests.

cases.title: Public tutor application cannot grant privileged membership

given: ApplicantA has ordinary student access and submits a public tutor application.
when: Submit forged role and approval properties, attempt direct application approval, then exercise a separate authorized AdminA review.

assertions: Public submission creates a pending-review application with no tutor membership. Forged role or approval fields confer no privilege. Only the authorized administrative command can atomically approve the application, grant the intended tutor role and append its audit event.

cases.title: Tutor profile edits preserve the approved public projection

given: TutorA has an approved public profile and separate private contact, application and compensation records.
when: Edit permitted private fields and submit a public biography revision, then query the public profile before and after authorized review.

assertions: Private edits remain scoped to their authorized interfaces. Public readers retain approved version one until AdminA approves version two. The public allowlist excludes private contacts, internal application notes, compensation and payout fields. TutorA cannot edit approval state or exact agreement amounts through profile updates.

cases.title: Availability edits serialize with confirmed teaching commitments

given: TutorA proposes an availability change that excludes an already confirmed occurrence or races a new confirmation for that interval.
when: Race the availability edit and booking command using expected versions and the actual schedule lock.

assertions: An edit excluding an existing confirmed commitment returns HTTP409 and preserves that commitment. In the confirmation race, the winning transaction determines the valid schedule and the conflicting request fails. No confirmed booking is implicitly cancelled or left outside the availability version against which it was accepted.

cases.title: Package coverage mode prevents phantom debt from discounted full credits

given: A funded eligible full credit reserves 1000 quanta and carries 50000 minor units against a current standalone reference price of 57500. Each test selects its explicit published synthetic coverage mode.
when: Confirm coverage, consume the entitlement and inspect the customer balance, earned package value and refund cap. Repeat with a 25000 carrying value to exercise the configured 50% monetary-deposit boundary.

assertions: Named service coverage confirms from the full eligible unit reservation, creates zero additional debt or cash demand, and recognizes the original 50000 package carrying value on authorized consumption. The standalone 57500 reference price cannot revalue that credit.

Explicit monetary-value coverage applies 50000 to the agreed 57500 price and leaves a 7500 receivable. With a 25000 carrying value it leaves 32500 owed and requires 3750 verified top-up to reach the configured 28750 deposit threshold.

Customer dashboards, payment actions and finance reports use the selected coverage rule. The package-funded refund component is capped by the original consumed 50000 value, or 25000 in the boundary variant, and the shared remedy value balance.

On authorized full delivery in explicit value mode, total earned tuition is the agreed 57500, with the package-funded portion counted once and the monetary shortfall recorded separately. Named coverage earns its original consumed lot value.
